mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-69.4 to -64.7), signalling that commuting routines are re-forming; returning commuters generate weekday foot traffic in retail corridors, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved every week from -69.4 at t-3w to -64.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES continues to improve week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing above -74.0 percent (it reached -73.0 at t-0w) breaks the suppressed-transit plateau; once transit use rises past that level, non-commute discretionary trips resume and pull RETAIL_REC up within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -74.0 percent change from baseline (it printed -73.0 at t-0w, up from -76.4 at t-3w).
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 3.4 points over four weeks to -73.0
failure_condition: TRANSIT stays above -74.0 for two consecutive weeks but mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days does not exceed its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL is falling (29.3 to 26.7) while GROCERY_PHARM is rising (-34.1 to -29.3); households are converting home-bound time into structured errand trips, and that errand routine spills over into adjacent retail-and-recreation visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 2.6 points while GROCERY_PHARM gained 4.8 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL keeps declining and GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising together.

mechanism_narrative: Under an announced-but-not-yet-effective staged reopening, both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve in anticipation of permitted activity; this anticipatory mobility converts into actual non-essential retail visits once the effective date passes, so RETAIL_REC is higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved jointly in each of the last four weekly means
regime_hint: staged reopening announced but not yet effective
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continuing to improve jointly.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS collapsed from +5.7 to -3.6 in the final week, ending the outdoor-substitution phase of the spring peak; as park-oriented leisure demand fades, discretionary footfall reallocates toward retail and recreation settings within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0 percent change from baseline after printing +5.7 at t-1w.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from -27.7 at t-2w to +5.7 at t-1w and back to -3.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the week after PARKS drops below zero is not higher than RETAIL_REC in the week PARKS was above zero.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stalled at -29.3 for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC improves by under 1 point per week; persistent provisioning behavior keeps trip budgets allocated to essentials, crowding out discretionary retail and pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM changes by less than 1 point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM held at -29.3 in both t-1w and t-0w
fact:RETAIL_REC gained only 0.9 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days exceeds its trailing 14-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains flat within 1 point.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of TRANSIT above -75 and WORKPLACES above -68, combined with RESIDENTIAL below 28, defines a synchronized out-of-home regime; when all three hold, retail corridors regain enough baseline foot traffic to lift RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT > -75 AND WORKPLACES > -68 AND RESIDENTIAL < 28 simultaneously (all three satisfied at t-0w).
failure_condition: All three thresholds hold for two consecutive weeks yet mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-enforcement regime where non-essential retail remains closed, the observed tentatively positive RETAIL_REC trend is measurement noise from essential-adjacent retail; retail and recreation mobility therefore stays flat-to-lower over the next two weeks rather than continuing to recover.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved only from -80.1 to -77.1 over three weeks while TRANSIT stayed below -73
regime_hint: tightened enforcement with non-essential retail still closed
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its trailing 14-day mean under unchanged closure rules.
